div.head: Af 21
div.ab: XVIIII. Gif preost oðerne mon ófslea, weorpe mon to handa ⁊ eall ðæt he him hames bohte, ⁊ hine biscep onhadige, þonne hine mon of ðam mynstre agife, buton se hlaford þone wer forðingian wille.
XIX. Gif preost oþerne mon ofslea, weorpe mon to handa ⁊ eal ðæt he mid him hames brohte, ond hine biscop onhadige, ðonne hine mon of þæm mynstre agife, buton se hlaford þone wer forðingian wille.

Be preosta gefeohte. Gyf preost oðerne man ofsléa, weorpe man to hande ⁊ eal þæt he him mid hámes brohte, ⁊ hine biscop onhadie, ðonne hine man of ðem mynstre agyfe, buton se hlaford ðone wer foreðingian wylle.
Si presbiter hominem occidat, capiatur et totum unde sibi mansionem emerat, et exordinet eum episcopus et tunc ab ecclesia reddatur, nisi dominus suus componere uelit weram eius.

[Be preosta gefeohte.] Gif preost oðerne mon ófslea, weorpe mon to handa ⁊ eall ðæt he him hames bohte, ⁊ hine biscep onhadige, þonne hine mon of ðam mynstre agife, buton se hlaford þone wer forðingian wille.
{XVIIII} Gif preost oðerne mon óflsea, weorpe mon to handa ⁊ eall ðæt he him hames bohte, ⁊ hine biscep onhadige, þonne hine mon of ðam mynstre agife, buton se hlaford þone wer forðingian wille.

Wenn ein Priester einen anderen Menschen erschlägt, liefere man [ihn] und alles, womit er sich eine Stelle kaufte, aus, und der Bischof degradire ihn, indem man ihn aus der Kirche herausgiebt: — es sei denn, dass der Herr [des Priesters] statt seiner das Wergeld [für den Erschlagenen] begleichen will.

If a priest slays another person, let [him] be handed over, and everything with which he bought himself a position, and let the bishop degrade him, handing him out of the church: unless the lord [of the priest] is willing to settle the wergeld [for the slain] in his place.

If a priest slays another man, he and all the share of the monastic property which he has bought for himself shall be given up; and the bishop shall unfrock him when he is ejected from the monastery and given up, unless the lord [of the monastery] is willing to answer for the wergeld [of the slain man].

If a priest slays another man, he is to be handed over, and all of the [minster] property which he bought for himself, and the bishop is to unfrock him, when he is to be delivered up out of the minster, unless the lord is willing to settle the wergild on his behalf.

If a priest slays another man, he shall be turned in as well as all that he bought for his home [in the church community], and the bishop shall defrock him when he is expelled from the minster, unless the lord is willing to negotiate payment of the wer [of the slain man].

note.label: same construction
note.quote: mon is not in all likelihood the object of weorpe but the agent of the transfer of property, as is made most obvious in the case of a fallen tree that crushes a man to death and is given to his kindred (cap. 13)

div.note: analogue Penitential of Theodore I.ix.8 The Penitential of Theodore (I.IX.8) mandates that members of the secular clergy be expelled from orders if guilty of homicide

analogue Penitential of Uinniau there is clear evidence from legislative analogues that have yet to be discussed in connection with Alfred’s code that encounters between priests guilty of homicide and their victims were not meant to result in the deaths of the former.

analogue Penitential of Columbanus (B 1) Instructions … for dealing with priests guilty of homicide are found in the penitentials attributed to the Irish abbots Uinniau and Columbanus … Differences between the two attestations are slight

analogue Paenitentiale Burgundense c. 1 Manuscripts of the Frankish Paenitentiale Burgundense and the subsequent Italian Paenitentiale Merseburgense a … contain just this provision … these canons potentially explain why … the priest is obligated (somewhat anomalously) both to compensate the kin of his victim and, apparently, to go into their power.
analogue Paenitentiale Merseburgense a c. 1 Manuscripts of the Frankish Paenitentiale Burgundense and the subsequent Italian Paenitentiale Merseburgense a … contain just this provision

analogue Wulfstan’s Canon Law Collection c. 102 a synthesis of a variety of penitential judgments on clerical homicide including that of Columbanus, does not reproduce explicitly the requirement of its source that the cleric guilty of homicide serve the parents of those he has wronged

note.label: same phrase (on hand gān)
note.quote: we have seen in the situation of the homicidal priest that to go on hand need not have had a lethal outcome. As this is the phrase used as well by the Alfredian clauses concerning sanctuary, we should seriously wonder whether the resolution they envision is similarly peaceful.

S. Gl Geistliche 12. 20. Der Schuldspruch ist bereits erfolgt; nicht etwa um ihn vors Gericht zu stellen, muss erst die Kirche ihn ausliefern. Phillpotts (Kindred 221) folgert irrig: ‘a priest is not expected to pay wergild if he slays a man’; vielmehr bleibt dies als der selbstverständliche Normalfall unausgedrückt, und wird nur der Fall der Zahlungsunfähigkeit des Priesters samt seiner Sippe hier angenommen

See Gl Geistliche 12. 20. Judgement has already been given; it is not, say, in order to bring him before the court that the church must first hand him over. Phillpotts (Kindred 221) wrongly concludes: ‘a priest is not expected to pay wergild if he slays a man’; rather, this, being the self-evident normal case, is left unexpressed, and only the case where the priest and his kindred alike are unable to pay is envisaged here

Kemble und Schmid möchten ‘und’ streichen gemäss Ld, der aber hierin vielleicht nur B’s moderner Änderung folgte. Auch Dial. Egberti 14 gibt dem als schuldig von der Kirche auszustossenden Geistlichen zurück res si quas ecclesiae optulerat, ut habeat unde se redimat

Kemble and Schmid would delete ‘and’, following Ld, who in this, however, was perhaps merely following B’s modern alteration. Dial. Egberti 14 likewise returns to the cleric who, being guilty, is to be expelled from the church res si quas ecclesiae optulerat, ut habeat unde se redimat
þæt hängt vom folgenden mid ab; mid feo biegað bei Toller. Ohne mid verstand wohl ‘was an Grundbesitz’ E; vgl. Koch Engl. Gram. § 380
þæt depends on the following mid; mid feo biegað in Toller. E probably understood it, without mid, as ‘whatever landed property’; cf. Koch Engl. Gram. § 380

ham Pfarrhaus; Ann. Agsax. 1129. Zum Genetiv (nicht ‘zu Hause’) vgl.: ic nyttes bycge in Salomo Sat. 202. So regiert earnian ‘erarbeiten, erringen, verdienen’ Acc. und Gen. Also kein Grund, ham oder hamas zu emendieren. ‘Pfrundhaus oder Platz in einem Kloster’ Schmid

ham parsonage; Ann. Agsax. 1129. On the genitive (not ‘at home’) cf.: ic nyttes bycge in Salomo Sat. 202. Likewise earnian ‘to work for, win, earn’ governs acc. and gen. So there is no reason to emend to ham or hamas. ‘Prebendal house or place in a monastery’ Schmid
Unkanonische Simonie s. Geistliche 12b—i; ‘was er eingebracht hatte’ (HB) ist späte Änderung kanonistischer Tendenz
On uncanonical simony see Geistliche 12b—i; ‘what he had brought in’ (HB) is a late alteration with a canonistic tendency

Nicht der Prozess, aber die Art der Urteilsfolge untersteht Geistlichem Gericht; s. d. Gl 9g. h. ‘Geistliche, die inter laicos gemordet, gehurt, gestohlen haben, dürfen a secularibus occupari, nisi animo fuerit ecclesiae pro talibus satisfacere’; Dial. Egb. 8

Not the trial, but the manner in which the judgement is carried out, is subject to the ecclesiastical court; see that word in Gl 9g. h. ‘Clerics who have committed murder, fornication or theft inter laicos may a secularibus occupari, nisi animo fuerit ecclesiae pro talibus satisfacere’; Dial. Egb. 8
Vgl. Gl Degradation 2—3. Der schuldige Geistliche verliert neben had auch eard (eðel, dignitas, liberalitas), d. h. Heimat, Landgut samt bürgerlichem Grundbesitzerrang; VIII Atr 26 = II Cn 41
Cf. Gl Degradation 2—3. Besides had, the guilty cleric also loses eard (eðel, dignitas, liberalitas), i.e. home and landed estate together with civil rank as a landowner; VIII Atr 26 = II Cn 41
‘dann’ Q, Editoren; agife wiederholt nur weorpe to handa. Af verhindert die Auslieferung eines noch Geweihten zur Blutrache
‘then’ Q, editors; agife merely repeats weorpe to handa. Af prevents a man still in orders from being handed over to blood-feud
Lord of the church; see Kirchenherr in Gl 6
Q scheint irrig des Priesters Wergeld als dessen Strafe zu verstehen; s. dagegen E Gu 3
Q seems wrongly to understand the priest’s wergild as his punishment; see, on the other hand, E Gu 3
nicht ‘für den Mann eintritt’ (Price-Thorpe, Toller 323); wie Land (s. Wb: geþingian), so kann man Busszahlung ‘dingen’
not ‘intercedes for the man’ (Price-Thorpe, Toller 323); just as one can ‘bargain for’ land (see Wb: geþingian), so one can bargain for payment of compensation

This cap. presents much difficulty. Liebermann adds ‘ihn’ after to handa, keeps and, reads mid him (following H, B, Ld, So), and bohte in preference to brohte (H and B). He translates weorpe...agife ‘liefere man (ihn) und alles, womit er sich eine Stelle kaufte, aus, und der Bischop degradire ihn, indem man ihn aus der Kirche herausgiebt.’ Hames (for mynsterhames, cf. cap. 2, above) however may be partitive genitive after þæt. Brohte (in H and B) seems to show that the meaning of the original was not clear.

note.label: himself
note.seg: Or “and everything with which he bought for himself a living” (or a place in a monastery). Thus Liebermann interprets it. In either case, the intention is to give the man his property for him to use it towards paying the wergild. Liebermann compares the Dialogue of Egbert, chap. 14, which, in treating of this very situation, says that the man cast out is to have any things he offered to the church “that he may have something to redeem him with”. Later MSS have “brought” for “bought”.
